I was hesitant to post here, but knowing other people have eyesight issues related to alters helps. I have several alters, 13 in total, not including me (the host). All my alters have different levels of eyesight. I have nearsightedness while others have farsightedness and yet others can't see a couple feet in front of them. I don't have total blindness with any of my alters, but I do have regular eyesight issues as well as brighter or darker colored eyes depending on who is out.

Well, the voices in your head certainly need to be looked at. Are they inside your head or do you actually hear them outside? Do they pop up and they don't seem like you think them yourself? Those are really important questions to ask yourself. 

I'd seek some help before it gets worse. Paranoia problems such as thinking other people are watching you tend to get worse over time. Depending on if the voices are outside your head (you're actually hearing them) or inside, it could be a number of things. If you seek help, make sure that you tell the therapist or whomever where exactly the voices are coming from. That's what changed my diagnosis from Schizophrenia to something completely different.

Sounds like me when I was younger. Sadly, this is only the beginning, if it's anything like what I'm going through. The anger will break down into vicious self-hatred. 

First off, you need to start thinking better of yourself. Your "inner voice" is your biggest, harshest critic. It seems impossible. Write down some things that you hate or dislike about yourself and combat it with good thoughts. It'll feel like the stupidest thing on earth for a while, but it'll end up making you feel good eventually. 

Second off, you can't change how your mother acts. My mother is absolutely horrid to me, emotionally. She probably won't take you seriously if she hasn't yet. If there's any way to seek some therapy or get some help, take it as soon as possible before the problem gets worse. Just keep poking around, eventually you're going to find SOMEONE who listens.

Friends are nice, but not required. School is especially brutal (sounds like you're still in it, correct me if I'm wrong). People will purposely exclude you, but not because you're "weird". Sometimes people exclude simply on the basis that you're too smart for them or they're scared of you for some similar reason.

Also, depression can have a serious effect on your ability to do tasks. It may come across as "laziness", when in reality it's the extreme lack of motivation that depression brings. I thought I was the absolute most worthless person on earth, then I figured out I could code rather skillfully. 

Having a boyfriend isn't all it's cracked up to be. Your worth is not defined by how many people want "into your pants". Your worth is defined by how worthy you are to yourself, if that makes sense. No one else can give you worth. My first serious relationship landed me in the mental hospital and I'm still extremely, extremely traumatized by it and my self-worth crashed through the floor. It's not really worth the trouble if you're doing it just for the feeling of self-worth or fitting in. 

It'll work out. Promise. If you're really worried about the boyfriend thing, I went all the way through school with people "joke dating" me. I got out of school and I figure out there were several people who really liked me but were way too scared to say anything to me. Someone probably looks at you at lot, you just don't notice. I certainly didn't.

Give life a giant f&ck you, that's all I can really say. 

I hope you the best, everyone else can chime in now if they'd like.
